draft.title: Average rate of change
card: The average rate of change of f(x) from x = a to x = b is how much f changes for each 1 unit of x, on average. It equals (f(b) − f(a)) ÷ (b − a).
This is the gradient of the secant, the straight line through the points (a, f(a)) and (b, f(b)) on the curve.
Worked example: for f(x) = x², find the average rate of change from x = 1 to x = 3. f(3) = 9 and f(1) = 1, so the rate is (9 − 1) ÷ (3 − 1) = 8 ÷ 2 = 4.
The answer is an average over the whole interval. The curve can be steeper or flatter at points inside it. If x and f(x) have units, the rate is in units of f per unit of x.
draft.remember: Average rate of change is the change in f divided by the change in x, which is the secant gradient.

a.q: For f(x) = x² + 2x, what is the average rate of change from x = 1 to x = 4?
a.why: f(4) = 24 and f(1) = 3, so the rate is (24 − 3) ÷ (4 − 1) = 21 ÷ 3 = 7. The answer 21 is wrong because it skips dividing by the change in x.
a.clue: Divide the change in f by the change in x.

b.q: A drone's height is h(t) = 2t² metres after t seconds. What is its average rate of change of height from t = 2 to t = 5, and what is it measured in?
b.why: h(5) = 50 and h(2) = 8, so the rate is (50 − 8) ÷ (5 − 2) = 42 ÷ 3 = 14. It is height per time, so the unit is metres per second. Answering 42 is tempting, but that is only the change in height and skips dividing by 3.
b.clue: Find both heights, then divide by the time taken.
